title: Logical Reasoning
description: Class 10 IMO — Logical Reasoning: number and letter series, analogy and classification, coding-decoding, direction and distance, blood relations, cubes and dice, calendars and clocks, and data sufficiency.

topics.title: Series, Analogy and Coding–Decoding
topics.concept: In a series, find the rule (difference, ratio, squares, alternation) and extend it. Analogy and classification ask which item shares — or breaks — a pattern. In coding–decoding, work out the letter or digit shift from the example and apply it.

examples.solution: Gaps 4, 6, 8 grow by 2, so the next gap is 10 → 30.

recap: Series: spot the rule and extend.
Coding: find the shift from the example, then apply.

quiz.q: The wheel that travels farther in one revolution is the one with the larger:
quiz.explanation: Distance per revolution equals the circumference.

quiz.q: Adding a constant to every observation leaves unchanged the:
quiz.explanation: Shifting all data keeps the spread (range) the same while moving the averages.

topics.title: Direction, Distance and Blood Relations
topics.concept: Direction problems track turns (left/right relative to facing); the straight-line distance from start to finish comes from Pythagoras. Blood relations are solved by sketching a family tree from the clues.

examples.problem: 3 km east then 4 km north — distance from start?
A's mother is B's sister — B is A's?

recap: Sketch directions; straight-line gap via Pythagoras.
Draw a family tree for blood relations.

quiz.q: If a quadratic polynomial has equal zeroes, its graph:
options: cuts the x-axis at two points
touches the x-axis at one point
quiz.explanation: Equal zeroes mean the parabola just touches the x-axis at a single point.

quiz.q: The minute hand of a clock sweeps a full circle in:
quiz.explanation: The minute hand completes one revolution in 60 minutes.

topics.title: Cubes, Calendars, Clocks and Data Sufficiency
topics.concept: For a standard die, opposite faces total 7; a painted cube cut into smaller cubes has predictable painted-face counts. Clock: the minute hand turns 6°/min, the hour hand 0.5°/min. Data sufficiency asks whether the given statements are enough to answer — not the answer itself.

examples.problem: A die shows 2 on top — bottom face?

recap: Opposite die faces sum to 7; minute hand 6°/min, hour 0.5°/min.
Data sufficiency judges whether the data is enough, not the value.

quiz.q: Which of these is always equal to 1?
options: tan θ · cot θ only at 45°

quiz.q: Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ for an AP equals:
quiz.explanation: Removing the sum of the first (n − 1) terms leaves the nth term.

questions.q: Multiplying every observation by 3 multiplies the mean by:
questions.explanation: Scaling all data by 3 scales the mean by 3.

questions.q: If c = 0 in ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0), then one root is:
questions.explanation: ax² + bx = x(ax + b) = 0 gives x = 0 as one root.

questions.q: A frustum can be seen as a large cone with a smaller similar cone removed from its:
questions.explanation: A frustum is the cone with the top (a smaller similar cone) cut off.

questions.q: If two lines in a plane are parallel, the system is:
questions.explanation: Parallel lines never meet, so there is no solution — the system is inconsistent.

questions.q: If the product of the zeroes of a quadratic is negative, the zeroes:
questions.explanation: A negative product means one zero is positive and the other negative.

questions.q: A tangent and a radius drawn to the point of contact are always:
questions.explanation: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the contact point.

questions.q: The measure most affected by an extreme value is the:
questions.explanation: The mean uses every value, so an outlier shifts it the most.

questions.q: If two solids have equal volumes but different shapes, then their surface areas are:
questions.explanation: Equal volume does not force equal surface area.

questions.q: A number is divisible by 10 if and only if it is divisible by:
questions.explanation: Since 10 = 2 × 5, divisibility by 10 needs both factors 2 and 5.
sin increases on 0°–90°, so sin 30° < sin 60°.
